subject: POC: Request to increase trial credits for large-context evaluation
messages:
From: Samira Kahn <samira@finovate.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: larger trial credit for Finovate POC (200k ctx)

Hi Hannah / Aditya,

Thanks again for the trial so far — the devs spun up the sandbox and the model is returning great quality. One wrinkle: our workload will routinely use documents in the 150k–200k token range (large legal contracts + linked exhibits), and our orchestration will generate sustained parallel streams at ~40–60 TPM during the initial evaluation. At the current default trial bucket we’ll exhaust credits within a day and can’t complete the automated evals.

Can Redwood temporarily increase the initial trial credit so we can complete a full run-through? What we’re asking for:
- bump to $2,500 in trial credits OR equivalent token allowance
- 60-day trial window (we need time to instrument metrics)

Attached is a short POC spec (POC_Specs.pdf) and our SOC-related checklist. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want more detail.

Thank you — Samira
Samira Kahn

Laura / Hannah — forwarding Finovate's ask. TL;DR: production-like POC with 150k–200k contexts and moderate sustained throughput (40–60 TPM). They want $2.5k credits + 60 days.

Why I recommend approving:
- Good fit: Finovate is a fast-moving fintech marketplace; if POC succeeds they’ve indicated a 3–6 month pilot to Dedicated capacity.
- Risk: modest — they are self-serve sign-up, no sensitive data planned yet (Dev cc'ed to confirm).

If you approve, I propose we either:
1) Issue a one-time promo code (FINOVATE-POC-2500) that the customer redeems in the console, OR
2) Apply credits directly to the trial account (preferred for speed).

Dev — can you confirm there are no blocking security flags for this level of trial credit? Monica — will CS pick up the onboarding if greenlit?

Thanks,
Aditya

Approve.

Conditions / notes:
- Approve $2,500 in trial credit + 60-day trial extension.
- Apply credits to Finovate's trial account (apply manually to avoid redemption delays).
- Dev: confirm logging & KV-cache retention defaults are acceptable for their workload; if they plan to send production data we need to ensure policy is followed.
- CS (Monica): prioritize a technical onboarding call within 48 hours of credit issuance; capture expected TPM and context distribution for Optimize recommendations.

Aditya — go ahead and coordinate issuance. Hannah — please add a short expiration note in the issuance email (credits expire 60 days from issue).

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Request: larger trial credit for Finovate POC (200k ctx) — credits issued

Hi Samira — quick update and confirmation.

Good news: Approved by Sales Ops. We have applied $2,500 in trial credit to the Finovate trial account (account email: trials@finovate.ai). Credits are visible in the Console now and will expire 60 days from today (2026-11-11).

Operational notes / next steps:
- Promo/manual application: applied directly to the account to avoid redemption friction. Promo code FINOVATE-POC-2500 has also been created in case you want to reuse it for additional engineers.
- Rate limits: We recommend starting at 50 TPM per project token bucket and increasing in coordination with our support team to avoid burst throttles.
- Optimize suggestions: once you run a representative workload, share TPM/context histograms with us and we’ll run a quantization + batching suggestion with expected cost delta.
- Security: Dev confirmed there are no immediate policy blockers; we recorded a note in the ticket for SOC review (see attached SOC2-Checklist.xlsx).

Attachments: credits-issuance.txt (summary of applied credit and internal reference FIN-3492)

Monica — can you schedule a 30–45 minute onboarding session with the Finovate eng team for tomorrow? Aditya — I’ll hand this to you for continued commercial follow-up.

Samira — let me know if you want me to raise Dedicated pilot options while you run the POC. Good luck with the run — please share the automated eval results once complete.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
